title: An AI Copilot Helps Engineers Design Buildings
summary:
Computers can design parts for airplanes, antennas, and race cars. But the best programs take a long time, and the human sees the finished design only at the end.

MIT researchers have built a fix: a system that works like an AI copilot for design. As the computer makes a structure, it shows the human the parts to change. Engineers also find it hard to trust designs that look strange.

The system uses topology optimization, a way of designing that finds the best shape for a structure. Until now, engineers had almost no control over how the design grew.

The researchers trained it on made-up examples of human feedback on thousands of designs.

In tests, the new structures were easier to make and 39 percent stronger against buckling, the way a structure bends and falls apart under pressure. It added only 15 seconds.

For now, users can only make parts thicker or thinner. The researchers hope to add more choices, and believe the system could open computer design to many more people, including students.
why_it_matters: The bridges you cross and the buildings you live in are designed by engineers, and if computers help them design better, those structures can be stronger and safer for you.
